doctor.orphan_tasks.body:
In github mode the queue is the repository ISSUES. The local queue should
  not exist, and while it exists there are two possible answers to
  "what is my next task" — which is what the exclusive mode avoids.

  Check if any are `claimed__` (work in progress) and remove the rest:
      ls .anchors/tasks/ && rm -rf .anchors/tasks/
doctor.orphan_changes.header: ⚠ %d delivery record(s) in `%s/` — and mode is `github`
doctor.orphan_changes.body:
In github mode delivery is recorded as a COMMENT on the card issue:
  that is where the reviewer looks, and it is the pipeline that moves the card to
  `ready-to-review`. A file here is read by no one — the watcher that
  would see it is not the mechanism in this mode.

  Each of these is a delivery whose DECLARED INTENT was never
  checked against disk — which is what the record exists to give.

  `anchors deliver` already records in the issue. For those left behind,
  post the content in the unit issue and move to `%s/`,
  or leave them as history from the period when mode was `local`.

  claim work, or repair the environment (protected branch, state
  labels). An agent cannot resolve this: login is interactive.

      gh auth login

  Then: `anchors doctor --fix` completes the rest.

  What `gh` returned:
  %s

status.first_plan_guidance:
→ NEXT STEP: project is assembled and has no work yet.

  The first plan is the FOUNDATION plan, and comes before any feature: without
  folder structure, linter, formatter and tests running, the first product
  plan runs into this on the first file — and each agent solves it their own way.
  It must answer, with what PROJECT.md decided:

    · where code lives — the tree declared in `anchors.yaml`
    · what formats and what lints, and the configuration for each
    · how tests run, and how the signal reaches `anchors ingest`
    · what CI executes on each push

  Run `anchors guide plan` for the rule.

  It is fine to write the entire SEQUENCE of plans at once — which allows
  reconciling scope between them — and release gradually: declare `needs:` in
  the header of each and commit only what can already be worked on. A plan whose
  `needs` has not finished does not become a card.

gate.scope_requires_run_or_check: gate of scope %s requires `run:` (external command) or `check:` (internal)
gate.judged_ai_failed: judged by AI: failed — see report issue
gate.judged_ai_waived: judged by AI: WAIVED — target question does not exist (declared `@TBD`)
gate.no_map_loaded: no map loaded — relational gate requires graph
gate.code_reference_valid.no_map: no map loaded — gate requires identity universe
gate.updated_at.no_git: no git repository — updated_at has nothing to compare against
gate.updated_at.uncommitted_diff: header updated_at (%s) ≠ today (%s), and file has uncommitted changes — update to date of change (%s), or run `anchors check --fix`.
gate.updated_at.no_commit: file without git commit (new/untracked) — nothing to compare
gate.updated_at.diff: header updated_at (%s) ≠ last commit date (%s). Update to %s (or run `anchors check --fix`).
gate.header.binary: binary file — identity is in name, not header
gate.header.executable_script: executable test script — identity is in file name and runner tags
gate.header.missing_block: missing `@anchors` header block — every graph file must have standard header at the top (see `anchors guide header`).
gate.header.recognized_missing_id: `@anchors` header without identity — recognized layer file (dao/infra/presentation/domain-types) must declare at least `layer: <layer>` (its minimum identity, as it has no spec). See `anchors guide header`.
gate.header.governed_missing_id: `@anchors` header without identity — declare `code: <CODE>` if this file is OWNER (the spec), or `ref: <CODE>` if referencing unit (rest of triad: code/feature/test). See `anchors guide header`.
gate.spec_sections.no_rules: spec without any rule/state CATALOGUED. Each rule needs a code and structured place — heading `### ABCDX-V01`, table row `| ABCDX-V01 | ... |`, or bold bullet `- **ABCDX-V01** ...`. (Loose prose mentions do not count.)
gate.siblings.empty_sections: EMPTY section(s) under cataloguing siblings: %s. Siblings (%s) have rules and these have none — and empty does not say if section DOES NOT APPLY or if nobody filled it. If not applicable, declare in the section itself: `@no-content: <why>` (section REMAINS, which matters when mandatory). If pending, write it.
gate.siblings.missing_code: section(s) without code under cataloguing siblings: %s. Siblings (%s) have codes and these do not — a rule without code is invisible to identity gates, and they report green on what they did not check. Give a code to each, or move text to prose section (`## Constraints`, `## Notes`) if not a rule.
gate.stale_test_signal: stale test signal (the spec changed since ingestion — reingest)
gate.stale_coverage: stale coverage (file changed since ingestion — reingest)
gate.no_coverage_baseline: no coverage baseline (ingest twice to compare)
gate.mutation.no_signal: no mutation signal ingested — line coverage says line EXECUTED, not that someone verified the result. Run mutation tool for your stack (Stryker/PIT/Infection/mutmut) and `anchors ingest --mutation <report>`
gate.mutation.stale: stale mutation signal (file changed since ingestion — reingest)
gate.mutation.isolated_failed: ISOLATED mutation score %.0f%% < %.0f%% — %s. %d mutant(s) survive unit's own test; %s
gate.mutation.failed: mutation score %.0f%% < %.0f%% — %d mutant(s) survived: code changes undetected by tests
gate.mutation.middle_range: mutation score %.0f%%: acceptable (>= %.0f%%), not yet desirable (%.0f%%) — missing %.0f point(s), %d mutant(s) still survive
gate.mutation.delta_high: full suite covers much more, so the gap is in unit test: dependents prove this unit, and a refactor here is not protected by local tests
gate.mutation.delta_medium: part of proof comes from dependents — in that slice, a refactor here is not protected by local tests
gate.mutation.delta_low: both scopes agree — gap is not coupling, it is assertions
gate.tests_pass.stale: stale result (test changed since ingestion — reingest)
gate.guide_checklist.missing_section: guide without '## Compliance points' section — without it judgment becomes heuristics. Distill rules into verifiable CK items (see `anchors guide guide`).
gate.guide_checklist.missing_items: compliance points section exists but has no 'CKn' items — list each verifiable point with its code (CK1, CK2, …).
gate.triad.skip_not_spec: not a spec — triad is checked on spec (the code owner)
gate.triad.test_desc: the test that proves the scenarios
gate.triad.incomplete: spec without complete triad — missing: %s. A spec alone passes relational gates (they have nothing to confront) and the pipeline certifies nonexistent work.
gate.triad.no_test_no_pointer:
spec declares `@no-test` but does not point to WHICH scenario proves this unit. The waiver claims behavior is proven elsewhere (central integration, e2e flow, consumer handler test) — and while that remains prose, the claim cannot be checked.

Cite scenario CODE in backticks within `@no-test` block, e.g.: `@no-test: delegates to handler, proven by `SGHBX-B01``
gate.triad.no_test_unresolved:
`@no-test` points proof to `%s`, but no project test mentions this code. An unresolved reference is worse than none: it gives the impression proof was verified.

Fix code, or write missing test
gate.triad.no_test_conflict:
spec declares `@no-test` but linked feature (`%s`) has %d scenario(s). Contradictory statements: waiver says nothing to prove, scenario says otherwise.

Pick one: write the test scenarios require, or remove scenarios (and feature, with `@no-feature: <reason>`) if behavior is not observable
gate.domain.skip: spec declares `@no-domain` with reason — receives no external input
gate.domain.skip_not_spec: the input boundary is declared on spec
gate.domain.missing:
spec does not declare `## Domain` nor waives the section.

Without either, nobody knows if unit has no external input or if nobody checked — and gate cannot distinguish the two.

Two ways out: open section declaring what unit ACCEPTS (one line per input, with who guarantees boundary), or waive with written reason:
    <!-- @no-domain: receives only typed props from internal code -->
gate.domain.empty: section `## Domain` is empty. Either declare what unit accepts (one line per entry), or remove section — an empty section ASSERTS someone looked and found nothing to declare, which is different from not looking
gate.domain.unowned: %d entry(ies) without owner in `Guaranteed by` column: %s. Name who blocks: this unit, caller, or interface
gate.spec_feature.skip_not_spec: obligation belongs to spec — it declares requirements
gate.spec_feature.skip_no_feature: spec has no linked feature (`covered-by`) — missing piece belongs to triad-complete gate
gate.spec_feature.skip_waived: spec declares `@no-feature` — without feature there are no scenarios to require from requirements
gate.spec_feature.skip_no_requirements: spec does not define coded requirement — nothing to cover
gate.spec_feature.missing: %d declared requirement(s) without scenario in feature: %s%s. A requirement without scenario traverses entire pipeline unverified. Write scenario, or waive on requirement line with `@no-scenario: <reason>`
gate.rule_implemented.skip_not_spec: spec catalogs rules — confrontation starts from it
gate.rule_implemented.skip_no_code_heade: spec does not declare `code:` in header — without identity there is nothing to confront
gate.rule_implemented.skip_no_rules: spec does not catalog any rule with code
gate.rule_implemented.skip_target_missin: code for this unit does not exist yet — absence belongs to `triad-complete` gate
gate.rule_implemented.marking_required:
none of the %d rule(s) of spec appears in code, and this project requires marking (`derived.rule_marking: required`).

Mark in code the snippet implementing each rule (`// %s-B01: …`) or waive on its line (`@no-mark: <reason>`). If NO rule has code, verify whether spec actually describes this unit
gate.rule_implemented.pending_migration: %d rule(s) cataloged and none declared — this unit precedes the rule↔code practice. When touching it, mark in code the rule each snippet implements (`// %s-B01: …`) or waive on its line (`@no-mark: <reason>`); then gate will confront for real
gate.rule_implemented.missing: %d rule(s) declared by spec and not implemented by code `%s`: %s%s. Implement them, or waive with reason (`@no-code: <reason>`)
gate.dependency.skip_not_spec: not a spec — only spec has Dependency Table
gate.dependency.skip_no_symbols: Dependency Table promises no confrontable SYMBOL (only prose description, or no dependency) — nothing to check
gate.dependency.pending_no_code: spec without linked code (specifies) — nothing to confront yet
gate.dependency.unused: Dependency Table promises symbol(s) that code DOES NOT use: %s. Either use promised symbols, or remove from table
gate.placeholder.unfilled: %d generator placeholder(s) unfilled: %s. Fill with real definition, or remove if not applicable
gate.count.stale: %d count(s) stale: %s. Update to match real count
gate.vr.missing: %d visual regression scenario(s) without baseline image: %s. Capture baseline image
gate.scenario.no_assert: %d scenario(s) with result step that does not assert result: %s. Result steps must assert outcome
gate.route.missing: SCREEN spec without declared route — add route line
gate.route.generic: navigation uses generic term — name concrete screen
gate.proof.boundary: rule(s) mentioning relationship with another unit WITHOUT marking `@cross-boundary`
gate.proof.missing_import: rule(s) asserting relationship with another unit without code IMPORTING target unit
gate.code_reference.invalid: cites %d code(s) that do not exist in project: %s.
gate.rule_types.invalid: uses rule type(s) outside canonical vocabulary (%s): %s. Declare the project vocabulary in `rule_types` in anchors.yaml (letter + term + sections), or use a canonical letter.
gate.rule_types.undeclared: uses UNDECLARED rule type(s): %s. Declare in `rule_types` in anchors.yaml (letter + term + sections) or use an existing letter.

section.purpose.route: NAVIGABLE screen: declares how one arrives at it. Without this the navigation graph is left with a loose node.
section.purpose.contract: Unit with DISTINCT input and output that deserve separate description (business rule, validator). Prefer `signature` when the function signature already says it all.
section.purpose.signature: PURE function whose input/output fit in a short table. Common in backend business-logic. Prefer `contract` when input and output need long description.
section.purpose.effects: Leaner alternative to `rules` for a unit without branching: lists what it causes, each item with its code. Prefer `rules` when there is a decision/conditional to catalogue.
section.purpose.domain: The INPUT boundary: which values exist, which are outside, and WHO guarantees the invalid never arrives. Unlike `constraints` (what the unit does not do): here one declares what it receives. Every unit with external input needs it — this is where the edge defects no gate catches live.
section.purpose.invariants: Truth that survives ANY sequence of operations — "writing V in month M ⟹ reading M returns V", "removing and restoring returns to the previous state". Unlike an effect (what one call does) and a constraint (the layer boundary). Every unit with a PRODUCER and a CONSUMER needs at least one: this is where the bugs that rule-by-rule testing misses live.
section.purpose.constraints: The layer boundary — what is someone else's responsibility. Applies whenever the boundary is confusable (e.g. a pure rule that does not fetch data).
section.purpose.errors: How the unit fails and who signals it. Use when there is invalid input, an external dependency or an impossible state to handle.
section.purpose.constants: Numbers/limits that are a business DECISION (plan ceiling, month window) — keeps the constant from becoming magic in the code.
section.purpose.state_shape: Store/global state: WHICH fields exist, of what type, with what initial value. Without this, the consumer discovers the shape by reading the implementation.
section.purpose.actions: Store: each action with its EFFECT on the state. The rule that decides the transition lives in business-logic; here goes what the action does to the state.
section.purpose.hydration: Store: what survives closing the app, from where the state is rehydrated and when. It is the source of stale-state bugs no unit test catches.
section.purpose.messages: Validation/form: the text the user READS when the rule rejects. It lives in the spec because it is a product decision, not an implementation one — and it is what the test asserts.
section.purpose.states: Unit with observable STATES (screen, state machine, hook with loading/error/empty). Do not use in a pure function.
section.purpose.state_flow: Unit with more than one state: what leads from one to another. Reveals unreachable states and dead ends — which the state-by-state list does not show.
section.purpose.loading: Unit that lists a COLLECTION that grows. Declare the strategy: all at once (and why the collection is bounded), paginated, or infinite scroll — and which piece implements it.
section.purpose.auth: Unit whose access depends on who the user is (permission, plan, data owner).
section.purpose.data_contract: Unit that DISPLAYS data coming from outside (query, parameter, store). Declares origin, whether required, format and default of each field. This is where date TIMEZONE and enum translation are declared — the two display defects no gate catches and that only surface in production.
section.purpose.data_states: Field with enumerated values or conditional origin. One item per VARIANT — it is what guarantees a scenario per branch instead of one for the happy path. Without it, a five-value enum becomes a single test.
section.purpose.navigation: NAVIGABLE unit: who leads to it and where it leads, each by CONCRETE NAME. It is what forms the navigation graph — a generic term ("the next screen") does not become an edge.
section.purpose.testids: Unit exercised by end-to-end tests. The stable identifiers the test looks for — renaming one breaks the flow and NO language tooling warns. Declaring them here makes the rename visible in review.
section.purpose.components: Unit composed of others already specified. Each piece in `backticks` becomes a verifiable CONTRACT; prose is not enforced. Unlike `deps` (what it consumes to work): here is what it is MADE of.
section.purpose.a11y: Unit with a form or complex interaction: label and hint of each element, focus order and keyboard behaviour. It is a legal requirement in many contexts — and a product decision, not an implementation detail.
section.purpose.props: COMPOSITION unit: everything that enters and affects what it shows or does. Each property with the values it accepts, whether it is required and the default. It is the contract with whoever composes it — the analogue of `domain` for an interface unit.
section.purpose.variants: Unit with AXES of variation (appearance, size, emphasis). One table per axis, with what each value changes. Without this, the combination of two axes is never enumerated — and that is where the combination nobody designed lives.
section.purpose.callbacks: COMPOSITION unit: what it emits outward, with the trigger and the firing CONDITION. It is the equivalent of navigation for what does not navigate — and the condition is the part people forget ("only fires if not disabled").
section.purpose.slots: Unit that accepts CONTENT from whoever composes it (children, named regions). Declares which regions exist and what each expects. Omit if the unit accepts no external content.
section.purpose.selectors: Global state: the DERIVED reads the consumer uses instead of recomputing. Declaring them here is what keeps the same derivation from being rewritten in each consumer and diverging.
section.purpose.history: The trail of who changed the spec and why. Applies where the spec is a contract between teams and the change must be attributable.
section.purpose.deps: What the unit consumes. Symbols in `backticks` become a verifiable CONTRACT (gate dependency-honored); prose description is not enforced.
section.purpose.open: What whoever implements will need and the spec does not answer. While an item remains here, implementing is guessing — and guessing is confronted by no gate, because all the pieces exist. Each question gets a CODE (`{CODE}-Q01`): without identity it neither becomes a traceable issue nor survives a rewrite of the spec. When the answer comes, PROMOTE it to a rule (with a code) and mark the item resolved citing the rule born from it; the question stays in the trail, it is not swept away.
section.purpose.notes: Non-obvious technical decision the code does not explain by itself (why this way, and not the expected one).

check.timing_note:
Wall time, this run, this machine — it varies with cache and load. Use it to
  compare gates with each other, never as an absolute budget. `worst` is the single
  most expensive confrontation, and it is what separates a gate that costs by VOLUME
  (cheap per target, times hundreds) from one that costs per TARGET. It is omitted
  where the gate ran once, since there it would only repeat the total.
